translationRepairs: He later served on the staffs of the generals who maintained the east and who guarded the army, became magistrate of Wen, rose twice to governor of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of colonel director of agriculture.

He later served on the staffs of the generals who maintained the east and who guarded the army, became magistrate of Wen, was promoted twice and became governor of Hongnong, and held the concurrent post of colonel director of agriculture.
再遷弘農太守 is the standard career formula of two further promotions culminating in the Hongnong governorship, not two separate tenures as governor.
After the abdication, Fu Xuan's noble rank was raised to viscount, and he was also given the title of chief commandant of attached cavalry.
After the abdication, Fu Xuan's noble rank was raised to viscount, and he was also given the title of chief commandant of attendant cavalry.
The chapter graph 附馬都尉 is the office 駙馬都尉, commandant of attendant cavalry; 'attached cavalry' is a false reading of 附. CText Jinshu keeps 附馬; Quan Jin Wen writes 駙馬都尉 for the same career step.

Fu Xuan submitted another memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Shun elevated five ministers, the realm was transformed through effortless governance because he put the right men in the essential posts."

Fu Xuan submitted another memorial: "Your subject has heard that when Shun elevated five ministers, the realm was transformed through effortless governance because he put the right men in the essential posts.
玄復上疏曰 opens a memorial that continues in the following units without a new speech verb; closing the English quotation at the end of this first sentence falsely ends the speech.
Therefore in the earlier edict I dared to have straight speech and nothing refused, hoping thereby to be able to air ignorance and mend faults, and obtain preservation of high rank.
Therefore the earlier edict allowed daring straight speech and forbade blocking it, hoping thereby to air ignorance and mend faults, and obtain preservation of high rank.
前詔敢有直言，勿有所距 is the emperor's earlier invitation that others dare speak frankly and that none refuse them, not a claim that he himself dared to speak.

Chen wrote to Xuan saying: "I have examined what your feet have written; the words are rich and the principles sustain; in ordering the threads of government it preserves and values Confucian teaching—enough to block the Yang and Mo schools' flow and evasion, and align Sun and Mencius with past ages.

Chen wrote to Xuan saying: "I have examined what you have written; the words are rich and the principles sustain; in ordering the threads of government it preserves and values Confucian teaching—enough to block the Yang and Mo schools' flow and evasion, and align Sun and Mencius with past ages.
足下 is the honorific 'you' addressing Fu Xuan; 省足下所著書 cannot mean that his feet wrote the book.
In the early Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed erudite of the heir apparent, and by stages was promoted to right assistant of the secretariat.
In the early Xianning era he inherited his father's noble rank, was appointed xianma (attendant) of the heir apparent, and by stages was promoted to right assistant of the secretariat.
拜太子洗馬 is the heir apparent's xianma post, not an erudite (博士) appointment.
Bearing sons is foolish; finishing official matters—official matters are not easy to finish.
Have a dull son and set him to finishing official business—official business is not easy to finish.
生子癡，了官事 is the proverb that a dull son should be left to finish official business; it does not say that bearing sons is foolish.

The sovereign was in mourning seclusion and listened to the chief steward, yet Yang Jun, lacking all propriety, at once played Yi and Zhou, thinking himself secure in possession of all under Heaven—this is why he died to the end.

The sovereign was in mourning seclusion and listened to the chief steward, yet Yang Jun, lacking all propriety, at once played Yi and Zhou, thinking himself secure in possession of all under Heaven—this is why he died.
所以至死 means this conduct is why he came to his death; 'died to the end' is not a reading of 至死 here.
I have done nothing dramatic, nor have I broken anyone’s power; why should anyone fear me?
I have been in office some days, yet I have made no striking move, nor have I made wings droop at the twang of a bowstring; who then will fear me?

The original drops 在職有日 and replaces 應弦垂翅 with invented 'broken anyone’s power'. The proposal restores tenure and the image, but 'snapped a wing as a released bowstring would' misstates the figure of birds' wings drooping when the string sounds.

In the fourth year of the Yuankang era he died in office at fifty-six. An edict posthumously restored his title as colonel director of retainers, granted one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and two hundred thousand cash, and gave him the posthumous name Zhen, "the steadfast."

In the fourth year of the Yuankang era he died in office at fifty-six. An edict posthumously granted him colonel director of retainers, one set of court robes, one suit of garments, and two hundred thousand cash, and gave him the posthumous name Zhen, "the steadfast."
詔贈司隸校尉 is a posthumous conferral of the office; 'restored' invents a prior stripping of the title.

This unit names only 元帝 as the summoner; Prince Langya is not in the Chinese and must not be inserted.

Zhi asked to go with Wu Mao of the secretariat to listen for news of the state, bowed and went down the steps.
尚書武茂 is Wu Mao as a secretariat official (尚書), not director of the secretariat (尚書令).
